data.gender_notes: Taraknath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Taraknath is a name derived from Sanskrit, which refers to the Lord of Taraka or the savior from all troubles. Tarakanatha is an epithet of Lord Vishnu and a manifestation of Lord Shiva. In Hindu mythology, Taraknath is believed to protect his devotees from all evils and grant them salvation. The name Taraknath carries the meaning “Lord of Taraka” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Taraknath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of taraka and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of salvation and protection.

It exemplifies the importance of faith and devotion in Hindu culture. The name carries a sense of strength and security, instilling confidence and reassurance in those who bear it.
data.spiritual_significance: Taraknath is a name aligned with the divine and the sacred. It embodies the idea of a higher power that is always watching over and protecting its devotees. vedic_reference.note: Taraknath is a popular name in Hinduism, derived from the name of Lord Taraka, who is considered the god of deliverance from all kinds of sufferings. In Hindu mythology, Lord Taraka is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to have the power to save his devotees from all forms of distress and misery. The name Taraknath is thus a reverential invocation to this deity, seeking his blessings for protection and deliverance from suffering.

historical_references.reference: Taraknath was a famous Hindu monk and a Jaina Tirthankara of the 11th century AD. He is believed to have lived during the 11th-12th centuries AD in Bengal, India. Taraknath was a renowned scholar and ascetic, and his teachings and works have had a profound impact on Jainism in Bengal and beyond.

Taraknath is also known as the 'Bengal Tirthankara' because of his prominent role in Jainism in Bengal. He is considered an important figure in the history of Jainism in India, and his teachings and writings continue to be studied and revered by Jains around the world.
historical_references.context: Prominent figure in Jainism in Bengal

modern_usage.modern_context: Taraknath is a popular name in Indian mythology, often depicted as a powerful god or demon in Hinduism. In the modern context, Taraknath is featured on various platforms including TV shows like Mahabharat and Chakravartin Ashoka Samrat, movies such as Jai Gangaajal and Sita: The Saga of an Emperor, and literature works like The God of Small Things and The Immortal Taraknath. These depictions often show Taraknath as a powerful and fearsome figure, reflecting the continued interest and fascination with Hindu mythology and its rich cast of characters.

name_in_real_life.story: Krishna Taraknath, a teacher in Hyderabad, India, shares that their name Taraknath meaning "Lord of Taraka" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
